title: Calibrate the Sensor
story:
From: Amara Okafor
Subject: sensor-sim needs real settings

The simulator reads its configuration from environment variables instead of a config file, because that is faster to tweak. It wants STATION, UNITS and INTERVAL. Without them it falls back to defaults and reports temperatures in furlongs. (Don't ask.)

Start a container named `sensor-sim` in the background with STATION=kestrel, UNITS=metric and INTERVAL=30. Until my real image is done, use `alpine:3.20` and this stand-in command, which echoes the settings it sees: `sh -c 'echo calibrated $STATION/$UNITS/$INTERVAL; sleep infinity'`
objectives: Run `sensor-sim` detached from `alpine:3.20` with `STATION=kestrel`, `UNITS=metric` and `INTERVAL=30` set
Use the stand-in command `sh -c 'echo calibrated $STATION/$UNITS/$INTERVAL; sleep infinity'` so the log shows `calibrated kestrel/metric/30`
startingState: No containers exist. Nothing is configured yet.
hints: Containers receive configuration through environment variables. You pass each one at `docker run` time, and the program inside sees it exactly as if it had been exported in a shell.
Use one `-e NAME=value` per variable, placed before the image name. Wrap the stand-in command in single quotes so your own shell does not expand `$STATION` first.

```bash
docker run -d --name sensor-sim \
  -e STATION=kestrel -e UNITS=metric -e INTERVAL=30 \
  alpine:3.20 sh -c 'echo calibrated $STATION/$UNITS/$INTERVAL; sleep infinity'
docker logs sensor-sim
```
solution: docker run -d --name sensor-sim -e STATION=kestrel -e UNITS=metric -e INTERVAL=30 alpine:3.20 sh -c 'echo calibrated $STATION/$UNITS/$INTERVAL; sleep infinity'
debrief: Environment variables let one image behave differently per deployment without rebuilding it. Pro tip: `docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Env}}' sensor-sim` shows exactly what a container was started with.
